newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- A controversial series of radio advertisements promoting the draft Security of Tenure Bill are to be withdrawn after an emergency meeting between SA Agricultural Union (SAAU) and Land Affairs Minister Derek Hanekom.

- An inquiry set up by Gauteng education MEC Mary Metcalfe to investigate irregularities in last year's matric exams issued a damning report on Tuesday on the provincial education department's handling of the exams, and recommended stern action against senior officials.
- The 1997/98 budget was expected to take a strong stand against leakages in customs and excise which lost billions in revenue, a tax expert said on Tuesday.

- Jaded investors looking for an exotic real estate option might be lured by the white sand and coral reefs of Paradise Island off the Mozambique coast, where leasehold righs are on sale for one million rand.
BUSINESS REPORT

- The Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP) Fund will receive a 4.4 billion rand boost in the March 12 budget, bringing the total allocated to the fund since 1994 to 19.6 billion rand, Neil Nel, the co-ordinator of RDP programmes, said on Tuesday.

- A multimillion rand customs scam uncovered recently involving South African and Namibian companies will not be fully exposed because Zavareh Rustomjee, trade and industry director-general, has allegedly called off a Customs and Excise investigation.
- Gencor, the minerals and metals group, was edging closer to becoming one of the top players in the aluminium market, Brian Gilbertson the executive chairman, said on Tuesday.

- A week rand and strong oil prices boosted earnings at Sasol, the petrochemicals-from-coal producer, but analysts had expected stronger earnings and the share price lost 250 cents to close at 51.50 rand on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD

- Sasol's attributable income increased 25 percent to 1,254 million rand in the six months till December 25 last year - despite the fact that import subsidies the synthetic fuel group receives dropped from 510 million rand to 75 million rand.
- Gencor lifted earnings for the six months to December by 49 percent to 60.2 cents per share.
- Another solid performance by the rand led rates on the capital market more than 20 basis points lower at one point yesterday.
THE STAR
- Wits Technikom became a casualty of student protests along with the University of Natal as unrest continued to sweep tertiary institutions on Tuesday.
- Seven Gauteng Education Department officials, including the province's third and fourth-highest ranked, are to be disciplined for the chaos surrounding last year's matric examinations.
- A 47-year-old Doornkop, Soweto, squatter camp resident shot and killed his son and wounded four of his other children before turning the gun on himself on Tuesday morning, police said.
- About 250 pupils went on the rampage in Atteridgeville west of Pretoria on Tuesday after police freed a suspected 24-year-old rapist who the pupils held captive for about five hours.
